questions.question: The sensation of sound persists in our brain for about
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1 s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **persistence of hearing** is the phenomenon where the sensation of a sound remains in the human brain for a short duration after the source has stopped vibrating.
 
• For the human ear, this sensation persists for approximately **0.1 seconds** (or **1/10th of a second**).
 
• This time interval is critical for the brain to distinguish between two separate sounds; if a second sound reaches the ear within **0.1 s** of the first, the brain perceives them as a single, overlapping sound.
 
• The concept of **persistence of hearing** is the biological basis for hearing an **echo**, which requires the reflected sound to arrive at the ear after the initial **0.1 s** period has elapsed.
 
• It ensures that sound signals are processed effectively by the **auditory cortex**, allowing for the continuity of speech and music perception without immediate decay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Echo and Minimum Distance**:

 
 
• To hear a distinct echo, the total distance traveled by the sound (from source to obstacle and back) must be such that the time taken is at least **0.1 s**.
 
• Given the **speed of sound** in air is roughly **344 m/s** at **22 degrees Celsius**, the total distance is calculated as **344 m/s × 0.1 s = 34.4 m**.
 
• Consequently, the **minimum distance** between the source of sound and the reflecting body must be half of this, which is **17.2 m**.
 
 
 
• **Reverberation**:
 
 
• In enclosed spaces like concert halls, sound may undergo **multiple reflections**. If these reflections reach the listener within the **0.1 s** window, they cause a prolonged sensation called **reverberation**.
 
• Excessive reverberation can make sound blurred or difficult to understand, which is why acoustic engineers use **sound-absorbing materials** like **perforated cardboard** or **heavy drapes**.
 
 
 
• **Auditory System Components**:
 
 
• The process involves the **outer ear** (pinna) collecting sound, the **middle ear** (ossicles) amplifying it, and the **inner ear** (cochlea) converting vibrations into electrical signals for the brain.

questions.question: The Eastern Ghats are also known by which of the following names?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nallamalai Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eastern Ghats** are a discontinuous and weathered mountain range that stretches along the **eastern coast of India**, running parallel to the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The **Nallamalai Hills** are one of the primary hill ranges that constitute the **Eastern Ghats**, located primarily in the states of **Andhra Pradesh** and **Telangana**.
 
• Geographically, these hills are located between the **Krishna River** and the **Pennar River**, forming part of the **Cuddapah Basin**.
 
• They are characterized by ancient rock formations including **quartzites** and **slates**, and they run in a north-south direction roughly parallel to the **Coromandel Coast**.
 
• Unlike the **Western Ghats**, which are continuous, the **Eastern Ghats** (including the **Nallamalai** range) are dissected by major peninsular rivers such as the **Godavari** and **Krishna**.
 
• The average elevation of the **Nallamalai Hills** is approximately **900 to 1,100 meters**, with **Bhairani Konda** being one of the highest peaks in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nilgiri Hills**:

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Blue Mountains**, these hills are located at the convergence of the **Western Ghats** and the **Eastern Ghats**.
 
• They are situated primarily in **Tamil Nadu**, with **Doddabetta** (2,637 meters) serving as their highest peak.
 
 
 
• **Rajmahal Hills**:
 
 
• These hills are located in the **Jharkhand** state and were formed from **volcanic activity** during the **Jurassic Period**.
 
• They form the northeastern part of the **Chota Nagpur Plateau**.
 
 
 
• **Maikal Hills**:
 
 
• This range is the eastern part of the **Satpura Range**, located in the state of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It acts as a **watershed** for major rivers including the **Narmada**, **Son**, and **Mahanadi**.

questions.question: Which plan was terminated one year before completion due to the Indo-China war?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961-1966) was designed to make India a self-reliant and self-generating economy, placing its primary focus on agricultural expansion and basic industries.
 
• The execution of this plan was severely disrupted by external conflicts, primarily the **Sino-Indian War (Indo-China War) of 1962**, followed shortly by the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1965**.
 
• These major defense crises forced the Indian government to divert crucial developmental funds toward defense spending and military stabilization, practically halting planned development.
 
• As a consequence of this structural disruption and severe inflation, the plan fell short of its targeted growth rate of **5.6%**, achieving only **2.4%**, leading directly to the implementation of **Plan Holidays** from **1966 to 1969**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956):**

 
 
• Formulated based on the **Harrod-Domar model**, focusing heavily on irrigation, dams, and the agricultural sector to address food shortages.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961):**
 
 
• Formulated based on the **Mahalanobis model**, emphasizing rapid industrialization, heavy domestic industries, and public sector expansion.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974):**
 
 
• Launched after the Plan Holidays, focusing on **growth with stability** and progressive achievement of self-reliance, which also witnessed the nationalization of 14 major Indian banks.

questions.question: The Chalukyas of Badami are noted for which contribution to Indian art?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rock-cut cave temples at Badami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chalukyas of Badami**, also known as the **Early Chalukyas**, ruled parts of southern and central India from the **6th to the 8th century CE**, with their capital at **Vatapi** (modern-day Badami in **Karnataka**).
 
• Their most significant contribution to Indian art is the creation of the **Badami cave temples**, a complex of four massive temples carved out of the local **red sandstone** cliffs.
 
• **Cave 1** is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and contains the iconic relief of an **eighteen-armed Nataraja**, which displays 81 different dance poses (mudras).
 
• **Cave 2 and Cave 3** are dedicated to **Lord Vishnu**; Cave 3 is the largest and most ornately decorated, featuring monumental carvings of **Trivikrama**, **Varaha**, and **Narasimha**.
 
• **Cave 4** is a **Jain cave** dating back to the late 6th or early 7th century, housing beautiful sculptures of **Tirthankaras** like **Lord Mahavira** and **Parshvanatha**.
 
• These caves represent a crucial evolutionary stage in **Indian rock-cut architecture**, serving as a stylistic bridge between the earlier **Ajanta-Ellora** traditions and the later **structural temples** of the Deccan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bronze sculpture of Nataraja**:

 
 
• This art form reached its zenith under the **Chola Dynasty** (9th-13th century) in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The Chola bronzes were created using the **lost-wax technique** (Cire Perdue) and are globally recognized for their aesthetic elegance and symbolic complexity.
 
 
 
• **Nagara style temples**:
 
 
• The **Nagara style** is the primary architectural style of **North Indian** temples, characterized by a **curvilinear shikhara** (tower).
 
• The Chalukyas of Badami primarily experimented with a hybrid style known as the **Vesara style**, which combines elements of both Nagara and **Dravida** (South Indian) architecture.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal and Aihole**:
 
 
• The Chalukyan era also saw the construction of major structural temples at **Aihole** (the 'Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture') and **Pattadakal**.
 
• **Pattadakal** is a **UNESCO World Heritage site** containing ten major temples, including the famous **Virupaksha Temple** built by **Queen Lokamahadevi**.

questions.question: National income measured at constant prices is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Real income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National income measured at constant prices**, also referred to as **Real National Income**, is the total value of all final goods and services produced by a nation in a year, calculated using the prices of a specific **base year**.
 
• By using **constant prices**, the calculation eliminates the distortions caused by **inflation** or **deflation**, providing a more accurate representation of the actual **physical output** and economic progress of a country.
 
• The formula to derive this value is: **Real National Income** = (**National Income at Current Prices** ÷ **Price Index of the Current Year**) × 100.
 
• This metric is vital for **macroeconomic analysis** as it allows for meaningful **long-term comparisons** of the **standard of living** and the productive capacity of the economy without being misled by nominal price fluctuations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nominal income**

 
 
• It is the **national income** measured at **current market prices** prevailing in the same year the goods and services are produced.
 
• It may show an increase even if **production volume** remains stagnant, provided there is a rise in the **general price level**.
 
 
 
• **Disposable income**
 
 
• This represents the portion of **Personal Income** that households actually have available to spend or save.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting **Direct Taxes** (like income tax) and other miscellaneous receipts of the government from the total income received by individuals.
 
 
 
• **Net factor income**
 
 
• Often termed **Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**, it is the difference between income earned by **domestic residents** from their factors of production located abroad and income earned by **foreign residents** within the domestic territory.
 
• It is the key variable used to convert **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** into **Gross National Product (GNP)**.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Which act first allowed Indians to be recruited into the Indian Civil Services through open competition in London?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1853**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1853** was a landmark piece of legislation that introduced a system of **open competition** for the selection and recruitment of civil servants in India.
 
• This act removed the discretionary power of nomination previously held by the **Court of Directors** of the **East India Company**, thereby ending the patronage-based entry into the services.
 
• The **covenanted civil service** was thrown open to **Indians** for the first time, allowing them to participate in the competitive examination conducted in **London**.
 
• This reform aimed to ensure that the **civil service** was staffed by individuals of high intellectual caliber and merit, regardless of their background or connections.
 
• The act also mandated a significant structural change by separating the **legislative** and **executive functions** of the **Governor-General’s Council**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Macaulay Committee**:

 
 
• In **1854**, the **Committee on the Indian Civil Service** was established under the leadership of **Lord Macaulay** to finalize the details of the recruitment process.
 
• The committee reinforced the principle that recruitment should be based on a high-standard **academic examination** rather than nomination.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1833**:
 
 
• This act attempted to introduce **open competition** but the clause was negated due to fierce opposition from the **Court of Directors**.
 
• It designated the **Governor-General of Bengal** as the **Governor-General of India**, concentrating power in a single central authority.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act of 1861**:
 
 
• This act introduced the **portfolio system** and included **Indians** as non-official members in the legislative councils.
 
• It marked the beginning of **representative institutions** by associating Indians with the law-making process.
 
 
 
• **Satyendranath Tagore**:
 
 
• He became the **first Indian** to qualify for the **Indian Civil Service** in **1863**, effectively utilizing the provisions established by the **1853 Act**.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the NAVYA program which was launched in June 2025?

options.text: To provide higher education to adolescent girls
To offer vocational training to adolescent girls aged 16-18
To promote sports among adolescent girls
To provide financial assistance to adolescent girls

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To offer vocational training to adolescent girls aged 16-18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NAVYA program**, officially launched in **June 2025**, is a specialized initiative designed to bridge the gap between secondary education and professional employment for young women.
 
• The program specifically targets **adolescent girls** in the **16-18 age group**, a critical demographic transition phase where many students drop out of the formal education system.
 
• Its primary objective is the provision of **vocational training** and **skill development** in high-growth sectors such as **Information Technology**, **Healthcare**, **Digital Marketing**, and **Textile Design**.
 
• By focusing on **employability**, the scheme aims to enhance the **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** among women and foster **economic independence** from a young age.
 
• The initiative aligns with the **National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF)**, ensuring that the training received is industry-recognized and provides **certified credentials** for the job market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vocational Training and its Importance**:

 
 
• Unlike **Higher Education**, which focuses on academic degrees, **vocational training** emphasizes **hands-on expertise** and technical proficiency in specific trades.
 
• It helps in creating a **skilled workforce** that meets the immediate demands of the **industrial sector** and the **service economy**.
 
• The focus on the **16-18 age group** is strategic, as it provides a professional alternative to those who may not wish to pursue traditional university education.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact**:
 
 
• By empowering girls with **market-relevant skills**, the program supports **Sustainable Development Goal 5** (Gender Equality) and **Goal 8** (Decent Work and Economic Growth).
 
• It acts as a deterrent against early marriages and financial dependency by equipping girls with the means to secure **sustainable livelihoods**.
 
 

Therefore, the primary objective of the NAVYA program is to provide vocational training to girls aged 16-18, making this the correct answer

questions.question: As of August 2025, how many Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) have been validated under NAMASTE scheme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**64900**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NAMASTE** scheme, which stands for **National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem**, is a specialized **Central Sector Scheme** designed to ensure the safety, dignity, and sustainable livelihoods of sanitation workers.
 
• As of **August 2025**, a total of **64,900 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs)** have been successfully **profiled and validated** through a rigorous identification process across various **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)**.
 
• The validation of these **64,900 workers** is a critical step in creating a national database that facilitates the delivery of targeted welfare benefits and **mechanized cleaning** equipment.
 
• The scheme focuses on the formalization of the sanitation workforce, transitioning them from hazardous manual practices to **mechanized sanitation operations** to achieve the goal of **zero fatalities** in sewer cleaning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Institutional Framework**:

 
 
• The scheme is a joint initiative implemented by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE)** and the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**.
 
• It replaces the previous **Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS)** to provide a more comprehensive safety net.
 
 
 
• **Core Objectives**:
 
 
• Providing **health insurance** coverage to all validated workers under the **Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**.
 
• Ensuring that all **Sewer and Septic Tank Workers** have access to **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)** and safety training.
 
• Offering **capital subsidies** of up to 5 lakh rupees to help **sanitation entrepreneurs** purchase specialized vacuum loaders and high-pressure jetting machines.
 
• The scope of the scheme has been expanded from 500 **AMRUT cities** to cover every **Urban Local Body** in the country.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is associated with the state of Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhortal Nritya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhortal Nritya** is a traditional folk dance originating from the **Barpeta** district of **Assam**, which is a major center for **Vaishnavite** culture.
 
• The dance was conceptualized and developed by the noted **Sattriya** artist and **Sattradhikar**, **Narahari Burha Bhakat**, based on the rhythmic elements of the **Sankari** culture.
 
• It is performed using large **cymbals** known as **Bhortal**, which are made of bell metal and weigh significantly, requiring dancers to exhibit great strength and agility.
 
• The performance is executed by a group of 6 to 10 dancers who create intricate **rhythmic patterns** called **Thok** while maintaining a fast-paced tempo.
 
• The choreography is highly **synchronized** and often represents symbolic movements like the swaying of boats or the flight of birds, reflecting the spiritual and natural heritage of the **Brahmaputra Valley**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gendi**:

 
 
• This is a folk dance associated with the **Gondi tribe** of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• Dancers perform while balanced on **bamboo stilts** (Gendi), moving through fields and villages during festivals like **Hareli** to celebrate the rainy season.
 
 
 
• **Kayang**:
 
 
• A traditional dance form from the **Kinnaur** region of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The dancers interlock their arms to form a chain like a **garland** (Kayang) and move in circular or linear formations to the accompaniment of local musical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Chakyar Koothu**:
 
 
• An ancient performance art from **Kerala**, traditionally staged in the **Koothambalam** (temple theater).
 
• It is a solo performance by the **Chakyar** community involving highly stylized **gestures**, facial expressions, and a unique **satirical narration** of stories from the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana**.

questions.question: In India, first census of coastal, wader birds kicked off in _____ in January 2025.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamnagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, India launched its inaugural dedicated **census of coastal and wader birds**, marking a significant step in avian conservation and migratory studies.
 
• The census was kicked off in **Jamnagar**, Gujarat, which is recognized globally for its vast **intertidal mudflats** and unique marine ecosystems that attract millions of birds annually.
 
• The exercise is a collaborative scientific project spearheaded by the **Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS)** in partnership with the **Gujarat Forest Department** to establish a baseline for **shorebird populations**.
 
• **Jamnagar** serves as a crucial hub along the **Central Asian Flyway (CAF)**, a major migratory route where birds from the **Arctic and Siberian regions** spend their winter months.
 
• The survey focuses on **waders**, also known as **shorebirds**, which are highly sensitive to changes in coastal health and serve as vital **biological indicators** of the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coastal and Wader Birds:**

 
 
• These species belong primarily to the order **Charadriiformes** and are characterized by long legs and specialized bills for feeding in **shallow water** and mud.
 
• Key species being monitored include the **Great Knot**, **Crab Plover**, **Sanderling**, and the **Bar-tailed Godwit**.
 
 
 
• **Marine National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the **Gulf of Kutch** near **Jamnagar**, it was established in **1982** as India's first **Marine National Park**.
 
• The park covers an area of approximately **163 square kilometers** and protects diverse habitats including **coral reefs**, **mangroves**, and **seagrass beds**.
 
• The region provides critical foraging grounds during **low tide**, where waders search for crustaceans, mollusks, and polychaete worms.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the 'Godachi Fair' traditionally celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Godachi Fair** is a significant socio-religious event celebrated annually in the **Godachi** village, which is located in the **Ramdurg taluk** of the **Belagavi** district in **Karnataka**.
 
• The fair is dedicated to **Lord Veerabhadra**, a fierce manifestation of **Lord Shiva**, who is the principal deity of the temple situated in this village.
 
• It is traditionally observed during the Hindu month of **Margashira** (falling between **November** and **December**) and reaches its peak on the **Poornima** (full moon day), attracting thousands of devotees.
 
• The **Sri Veerabhadra Swamy Temple** at Godachi is historically significant, featuring architectural elements that represent a blend of the **Chalukyan** and **Vijayanagara** eras.
 
• This fair serves as a vital cultural gathering for the people of **North Karnataka**, involving various traditional rituals, local commerce, and folk performances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gujarat**:

 
 
• Famous for the **Tarnetar Mela**, which is a significant tribal fair celebrated at the **Trinetreshwar Mahadev** temple near **Thangadh**.
 
 
 
• **Assam**:
 
 
• Known for the **Ambubachi Mela** held at the **Kamakhya Temple** in **Guwahati**, which celebrates the presiding goddess of the temple.
 
 
 
• **Haryana**:
 
 
• Renowned for the **Surajkund International Crafts Mela** in **Faridabad**, which showcases the rich diversity of Indian handicrafts, handlooms, and cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Belagavi District**:
 
 
• Known as the **Sugar Bowl of Karnataka**, it is a hub for diverse cultural festivities, including the **Kittur Utsav** and various regional **Jatras**.

questions.question: As per census 2011, what is the literacy rate of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**94.00%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **2011 Census**, **Kerala** remains the most literate state in **India** with a total literacy rate of **94.00%**.
 
• The state exhibits a high level of educational attainment across genders, with **male literacy** recorded at **96.11%** and **female literacy** at **92.07%**.
 
• **Kerala** has a long history of social reform movements and government initiatives, such as the **Total Literacy Campaign**, which contributed to achieving this milestone.
 
• The gap between male and female literacy in the state is among the narrowest in the country, reflecting a high degree of **gender equality** in access to education.
 
• Educational development in **Kerala** is supported by a robust network of **government-aided schools** and a high priority on primary education in state budgeting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Literacy Statistics (2011 Census)**:

 
 
• The average literacy rate of **India** was **74.04%**.
 
• The national **male literacy rate** stood at **82.14%**, while the **female literacy rate** was **65.46%**.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Comparisons**:
 
 
• **Bihar** was identified as the state with the lowest literacy rate at **61.80%**.
 
• Among Union Territories, **Lakshadweep** recorded the highest literacy rate at **91.85%**.
 
• The state of **Mizoram** ranked second in literacy with a rate of **91.33%**.
 
 
 
• **Census Definition of Literacy**:
 
 
• For the purpose of the **Census 2011**, a person aged **7 years and above** who can both read and write with understanding in any language is considered literate.

questions.question:
In Southern Indian states, Rice is cultivated in which of the following season?

I. Rabi II. Kharif
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rice cultivation in **Southern India** is not restricted to a single season due to the prevailing **tropical climate** and availability of **irrigation facilities**. In the **Rabi** season, which typically spans from **November to April**, rice is extensively grown in states like **Andhra Pradesh**, **Tamil Nadu**, and **Telangana**, where it is often referred to by local names such as **Dalwa** or **Navarai**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Kharif** season, running from **June to October**, is the primary cropping season for rice across the country, including the **Southern states**. This season coincides with the **Southwest Monsoon**, providing the necessary high rainfall and **humidity** required for the initial growth phase of the paddy crop. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice Cultivation Profile:**

 
 
• **Climatic Requirements:** Rice is a **tropical crop** that requires high temperatures, generally above **25 degrees Celsius**, and high humidity. It necessitates an annual rainfall of over **100 cm**; in areas with less rainfall, it is grown with the help of **canal irrigation** and **tube wells**.
 
• **Soil and Geography:** The most suitable soil for rice is **alluvial soil** with a **clayey base** that can retain water. India is the **second-largest producer** of rice globally, with **West Bengal**, **Uttar Pradesh**, and **Punjab** being leading producers alongside Southern states.
 
• **Cropping Patterns:** In certain regions like **West Bengal** and the **Brahmaputra Valley**, three crops of paddy are grown in a single year, known as **Aus**, **Aman**, and **Boro**.
 
• **Agricultural Methods:** Cultivation involves various methods such as **transplanting** (most common), **broadcasting**, and the **drilling method**, often requiring significant **manual labor**.

questions.question: In which year was the Volleyball Federation of India formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Volleyball Federation of India (VFI)** is the supreme governing body for the sport of volleyball in India, and it was officially established in the year **1951**.
 
• Prior to the formation of the federation, the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** controlled the sport in the country from **1936 to 1950**, organizing interstate championships every two years.
 
• The first **National Championship** for men under the newly formed VFI was held in **1952** at **Ludhiana**, marking a significant milestone in the structured development of the game in India.
 
• The federation is affiliated with the **Federation Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB)** and the **Asian Volleyball Confederation (AVC)**, ensuring India's participation in global and continental events.
 
• Following the establishment of the VFI, the **National Championship for Women** was also introduced, starting in **1953**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Governance and Context:**

 
 
• The **Federation Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB)**, the global administrative body for the sport, was founded in **April 1947** in Paris and is currently headquartered in **Lausanne**, Switzerland.
 
• Volleyball was introduced to the **Asian Games** for the first time in **1958** during the Tokyo edition, where the **Indian Men's Team** secured a **Gold Medal**.
 
• The sport attained **Olympic status** during the **1964 Tokyo Olympics**, further boosting the professionalization efforts of national federations like the VFI.
 
• In India, the **Volleyball Federation of India** oversees various formats, including **Indoor Volleyball** and **Beach Volleyball**, and manages the **Prime Volleyball League** to enhance the sport's domestic popularity.

questions.question:
The given below skill is called "Toe touch" that is related to which of the following sports?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e01b4ebd132a17d8bee2d5950064daa03a72b7e608cb87cc1c18e62a01739669.png]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabaddi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Kabaddi**, the **Toe touch** is a vital **offensive skill** used by the **raider** to touch an **anti** (defender) using their foot while maintaining a safe distance.
 
• The technique requires the **raider** to extend their leg rapidly to tag the **defender's foot** or **lower leg** with the **toes**, allowing them to score a point without getting deep into the opponent's territory.
 
• Successful execution of a **toe touch** relies heavily on **agility**, **flexibility**, and **timing**, as the **raider** must be prepared to retract their leg immediately to avoid an **ankle hold**.
 
• This move is often used to surprise **defenders** who are focused on the **raider's** upper body movements, hand reach, or lateral shifting during the **raid**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Beyond the **toe touch**, **Kabaddi** involves several other technical skills classified into offensive and defensive maneuvers:

 
 
• **Hand Touch:** An offensive move where the **raider** extends their arm to touch a **defender**; variations include the **running hand touch** and **turning hand touch**.
 
• **Dubki:** A specialized move where the **raider** escapes a **chain tackle** by ducking low beneath the defenders' arms.
 
• **Frog Jump:** An athletic move where the **raider** jumps over the **defensive line** to escape a **thigh hold** or **block**.
 
• **Ankle Hold:** A fundamental **defensive skill** where a **corner defender** captures the **raider's ankle** to prevent them from reaching the **mid-line**.
 
• **Bonus Line:** A technical line in **Kabaddi**; a **raider** can earn a **bonus point** by crossing this line with one foot while the other is in the air, provided there are at least **6 or 7 defenders** on the mat.

questions.question: Global Business Complexity Index 2025 was published by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TMF Group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Business Complexity Index (GBCI)** is an authoritative annual report that provides an in-depth analysis of the global and local environments for **business compliance** and administration.
 
• The report is published by **TMF Group**, a leading global provider of high-value business services to organizations operating and investing globally.
 
• The 2025 edition continues to rank various jurisdictions (typically around **79 jurisdictions**) based on their complexity for multinational companies to operate in, covering **accounting**, **tax**, **payroll**, and **legal compliance**.
 
• The index uses a **quantitative and qualitative methodology**, aggregating thousands of data points across factors such as **regulatory changes**, **technological adoption**, and **geopolitical stability**.
 
• It serves as a benchmark for **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** decisions by highlighting how different regions manage **transparency** and **digitalization** in business processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **TMF Group**:

 
 
• Headquartered in **Amsterdam, Netherlands**, it assists businesses in navigating the **legal and regulatory requirements** of over 80 jurisdictions.
 
• It focuses on helping companies manage **entity life cycles** and **cross-border expansion**.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**:
 
 
• A major financial agency of the **United Nations** that publishes the **World Economic Outlook** and the **Global Financial Stability Report**.
 
• It focuses on **macroeconomic stability** and **poverty reduction** rather than specific business administrative complexity.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**:
 
 
• The global body overseeing the **rules of international trade** between member nations.
 
• It is primarily concerned with **trade barriers**, **tariffs**, and **dispute settlement**.
 
 
 
• **Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU)**:
 
 
• A research and analysis division that produces the **Democracy Index** and **Global Liveability Index**.
 
• It provides **country risk assessments** and **economic forecasting** services.

questions.question: Government has notified National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for 12 pollutants in ___ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** were revised and notified by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in **November 2009**, replacing the previous standards from 1994.
 
• These standards are formulated under the **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**, which empowers the central government to set limits on pollutants to protect public health and the environment.
 
• The 2009 notification specifically listed **12 pollutants** to be monitored: **Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)**, **Particulate Matter (PM10)**, **Particulate Matter (PM2.5)**, **Ozone (O3)**, **Lead (Pb)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Ammonia (NH3)**, **Benzene**, **Benzo(a)pyrene**, **Arsenic**, and **Nickel**.
 
• A major shift in the **2009 standards** was the adoption of uniform air quality limits across **industrial**, **residential**, and **rural areas**, whereas previous versions had different permissible limits for different land-use categories.
 
• The monitoring of these pollutants is essential for the **National Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP)**, which tracks the status of air quality in various cities across **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**:

 
 
• It is a **statutory organization** constituted in **September 1974** under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**.
 
• It provides technical guidance to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** and coordinates the activities of **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)**.
 
 
 
• **National Air Quality Index (AQI)**:
 
 
• Launched in **October 2014**, the **AQI** is a tool to communicate air quality status to people in terms that are easy to understand (e.g., Good, Satisfactory, Poor).
 
• While **NAAQS** monitors 12 pollutants, the **AQI** focuses on **eight major pollutants**: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb.
 
 
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**:
 
 
• This was launched in **January 2019** as a long-term, time-bound strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across the country.
 
• It targets a **20−30% reduction** in **PM2.5** and **PM10** concentrations by **2024**, taking 2017 as the base year for comparison.
